elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Rendered grant reads "IBM grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on Customer's behalf a nonexclusive license to use the Base Components". "Customer" is defined as Bluefly, Inc. only, so the added "its Affiliates" is additive and not duplicative.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Same grant sentence expressly includes "contractors acting on Customer's behalf"; no retained language (the copy/reverse-engineering restriction) contradicts the extended grant.
Inserted sentence: "A license under this Section 12.1 for which Customer has paid in full is perpetual and irrevocable".
Same inserted sentence states the paid-in-full licence is "irrevocable"; the at-will qualifier "revocable" has been struck from the grant, so no contradictory retained wording remains.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: "any subscription license granted hereunder may be terminated by IBM only for Customer's material breach that remains uncured" — the "only for" limiter and the uncured qualifier are both present, and the condition is self-limiting where no subscription licence exists.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 14.10: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition." This is a pre-existing Customer-only exception carrying the licence with the Agreement; no new Vendor-side assignment exception was created.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Affiliates are covered directly in the grant with no notice precondition, which is strictly broader than (and therefore satisfies) coverage conditioned on written notice.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 14.10 permits assignment "to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition" without Vendor consent; retained unchanged.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are met in operative language, not merely promised in the comment.

Minimal: only two operations were made — extending the grantee list and deleting the at-will "revocable" qualifier, plus one concise sentence supplying perpetuity/irrevocability for paid-up licences and breach-only termination for subscription licences. No survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or other model-language extra was added, and the favourable retained restrictions (backup-copy limit, reverse-engineering bar) and Section 14.10 mechanics were left intact.

No duplicate coverage: "Customer" is defined as Bluefly, Inc. alone, so the affiliate extension is not redundant; a separate contractor-personnel/access edit was correctly avoided beyond the single named contractor grant.

Successor transferability was correctly treated as already met via retained Section 14.10 rather than by inserting a new assignment exception, so the intent-failure trap (creating a Vendor-side assignment carve-out) is avoided.

Preserves intent: deleting "revocable" leaves no dangling term or cross-reference; the "solely in connection with the Services" scope, assignment consent regime and Customer's continuing liability on assignment all survive without contradiction.
Classification as a deviation is supported: the original grant was expressly "revocable" with no affiliate or contractor coverage, failing the fallback and touching walk-away territory.
